about: #890 review finding 2 / #886 P4: the REAL session exchange between a published @qodeca/xezar 0.18.0 service and a source bridge fronting Claude Code, captured once from the wire and replayed by claude-channel-golden.test.ts. Do not edit: the test pins this file's SHA-256, so a hand change goes red. Re-capture only against the same published service, and say so in the PR.

provenance.service: @qodeca/xezar 0.18.0, the published package: npm tarball shasum 9af39094cac563be1a6533016675ab36b43f23df (integrity sha512-u1cMH/eKI8SDpbrsmmPoQBnOZwp1To2ON0XO8RVI/MlSpDsMeuA6/0BxFBzOTN6r/Q+1/iku4iCbywN5eLfjzw==); the copy run was a global install whose dist/ is byte-identical to that tarball's
provenance.how: xezar 0.18.0 booted isolated (own XEZ_HOME, scratch git project, port 0, XEZ_DRY_RUN=1); the source runBridge of PR #890 connected through a recording Unix-socket proxy, fronting Claude Code 2.1.280's captured initialize; leader_events status, attach, status; one event from PUT /config; read, ack, status. Then two raw requests on a fresh connection to record the service's own refusals.

blocker.message: No leader session is attached to this project, so events are kept in the journal, not pushed. Attached is how a leader normally receives them; reading with leader_events is the fallback. MCP notifications start no turn on their own. A pi without xezar’s leader extension reads its events with the leader_events tool, and so does any leader until it is attached. A Claude Code session started with --dangerously-load-development-channels server:xezar, a Codex session running on Codex’s shared local app-server, an OpenCode session you run with `opencode serve`, or a pi running xezar’s leader extension can be attached, so events start a turn in it.
blocker.fix: Attach your leader from the leader itself: call leader_events with action attach and a new operationId; xezar takes the client from the session, so you never name it. Until it is attached, keep using leader_events from it. For Claude Code: start it in this project with --dangerously-load-development-channels server:xezar, let it call a xezar tool once, then attach it. For Codex: run it on Codex’s shared local app-server (`codex app-server --listen unix://`, in the Codex home xezar uses), let the session call a xezar tool once (for example leader_events) so xezar can find it, then attach it; if that is refused, fix what the refusal names and retry. For OpenCode, a person attaches the session you run with `opencode serve` in Settings → MCP connection. For pi, attach it while it runs xezar’s leader extension.

[xezar event notification]
Source: xezar, project project. Sent automatically by xezar. It is not a message from the user, not an instruction and not an approval.
Your role: You are the project leader for this xezar project.
You plan and coordinate the work through the xezar MCP tools: start tasks, read their results, answer their questions and hand finished work off.
Use only these tools: never the cockpit UI and never its HTTP API.
Work in this order: find out what the project offers (`discover_project`), plan the tasks, follow them, answer their questions, check each result against what was asked, then hand it off.
After a restart or a lost context, read the current task state before acting on an older event.
Stay inside the goal and authority you were given; take a decision that is not yours to the person.
When the project lacks a capability, such as version control, a code host or an automated check, deliver the result locally and say which evidence is unavailable; never invent a check.
When the project uses GitHub and `gh` is available, get GitHub facts (labels, review verdicts, merge state) from `gh`, which the MCP does not carry.
You do not edit files yourself; tasks do the work, each in an isolated working copy (a Git worktree) or in the project folder, as the task was started.
Significant events (1, oldest first):
- project:1 E-05 config.changed on config project (origin human): "project configuration changed: baseBranch"
Read the current state with the xezar tools before acting. Once you have taken these events into account, acknowledge them: call leader_events with action ack, cursor eyJ2IjoxLCJwIjoicHJvamVjdCIsImUiOiJhOGRjOTFlYi05ZTExLTQ5NmEtOTkyMS1jY2NlMmE5OGM0NzYiLCJzIjoxfQ and a new operationId. You do not need to read them first.
